rfm_tuples.R: We anticipate submitting a final external audit to the FDA by the end of the first quarter of 2024 with commercialization targeted for the second half of 2024. (10-K Item 7, FDA Matters, regarding Boston facility resumption)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify the 10-K's stated H2 2024 commercialization timeline is reaffirmed in the next 10-Q (Q1 2024 filed 2024-05-06). Mode B: derive that an external audit by a third party will produce findings that may extend the timeline; check for any in-period revision.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2024 10-Q (0000917520-24-000061, filed 2024-05-06) Item 2 MD&A, Boston facility / FDA Matters section; cross-reference 10-K language
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2024 10-Q: 'While we anticipated this audit would yield findings and there would be remaining work to be completed, the audit yielded more findings than we anticipated. We are still determining the full scope of the work required to address these additional findings and resume commercial distribution... do not expect to resume commercial distribution in 2024.' Same quarter the Company recorded a $7.1M definite-lived customer-relationship intangible impairment (SurgiMend/PriMatrix) and ran a quantitative goodwill test on the TT reporting unit (20% headroom at Q1 2024 vs. >20% in 10-K qualitative).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Highly material claim evolution within ~67 days of the 10-K. Management's confident H2 2024 commercialization timeline in the 10-K was contradicted by the very next 10-Q, which explicitly removed 2024 from the resumption guidance and triggered an interim impairment. This is the strongest single signal in the file: the disclosed remediation pace in the 10-K did not survive into Q1 2024.

rfm_tuples.R: Following implementation of upgraded Good Laboratory Practices and expertise and a standardization of corrective and preventative action processes and governance, the Company resumed manufacturing at its Boston facility in the fourth quarter of 2023. (10-K Item 7)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify manufacturing resumption is real (registry / 10-Q reaffirmation). Mode B: derive that 'resumed manufacturing' is distinct from 'resumed commercial distribution'; products made under quarantine pending FDA clearance are not revenue-bearing. Check that the carrying value of related intangibles supports the timing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 7 (Goodwill / Intangibles) and Q1 2024 10-Q Note 5 (Goodwill / Intangibles) — SurgiMend $38.3M and PriMatrix $27.7M carrying values; $7.1M customer-relationship impairment recorded Q1 2024
rfm_tuples.M_value: Manufacturing resumption confirmed by both filings, but Q1 2024 10-Q clarifies that commercial distribution has NOT resumed and the TT reporting unit goodwill ($388.5M of $1,055M total) required a quantitative test in Q1 2024 (vs. qualitative in the 10-K). 10-K stated 'more than 20% headroom' qualitatively for TT; Q1 2024 quantitative test produced exactly 20% headroom — i.e., headroom did not expand and the test was upgraded in rigor.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: 10-K framing of 'resumed manufacturing in Q4 2023' is technically true but creates an inference of restored cash flows that the disclosure of zero commercial distribution and $7.1M impairment immediately undercuts. TT goodwill ($388.5M) is the leveraged tail risk; 20% headroom is non-trivial cushion but is calibrated to the optimistic resumption timeline the Company has already walked back.

rfm_tuples.R: At March 31, 2024, the Company was in compliance with all such covenants. (Q1 2024 10-Q Note 6, Senior Credit Facility) — supported by 10-K disclosure that the March 2023 Amendment widened the maximum consolidated total leverage ratio to 4.50x through 12/31/2024, then steps to 4.25x and 4.00x.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm compliance per the credit agreement schedule. Mode B: derive that a covenant amendment widening the leverage ceiling to 4.50x for ~21 months is itself a distress signal even when current compliance is true.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 5 Debt + Q1 2024 10-Q Note 6 Debt — Seventh Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (March 2023 Amendment); also December 2023 Amendment of the Securitization Facility extending maturity from May 2024 to December 2026
rfm_tuples.M_value: Compliant. But March 2023 amendment widened the covenant; April 2023 and December 2023 amendments stretched the receivables securitization maturity. $1.4B total external debt at 12/31/2023. Acclarent acquisition closed 4/1/2024 for $275M cash plus $5M regulatory milestone (funded by Senior Credit Facility per management's stated funding plan). Step-down to 4.25x begins Q1 2025.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: covenant ceiling was relaxed to 4.50x precisely because management foresaw EBITDA pressure from the Boston recall and the Acclarent levering acquisition. Compliance today is not a meaningful pass — the relevant question is the Q1 2025 step-down to 4.25x and the TTM EBITDA trajectory after Acclarent integration, given Boston revenue has not returned.

rfm_tuples.R: Our consolidated financial statements have been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm... We have served as the Company's auditor since 1989. (10-K Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm)

The PwC CAM on TT goodwill is itself a useful Mode B pointer: the auditor flagged the same asset that subsequently required an interim quantitative test in Q1 2024. rfm_tuples.R: Our management... concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2023. (10-K Item 9A)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify Item 9A conclusion and PwC ICFR opinion. Mode B: derive whether the Boston facility quality-system breakdown (which prompted the Warning Letter and global recall) should have surfaced as a material weakness in product-quality-related controls feeding revenue recognition, returns provision, and intangible asset impairment estimates.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9A + PwC ICFR opinion + Q1 2024 10-Q disclosures
rfm_tuples.M_value: ICFR concluded effective by management and PwC. However, the FDA's 2023 Form 483 and July 2023 Warning Letter, the $18.7M product returns provision recorded in connection with the global recall, and the $7.1M intangible impairment recorded in Q1 2024 (driven by an external audit finding more issues than management forecasted) all live downstream of the same quality-system control environment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: FDA quality-system controls are technically distinct from ICFR over financial reporting, so a clean 9A is not a contradiction. Mode B: investors should still discount the precision of management's TT-segment forecasts given the same engineering organization produced the quality failures that led to the recall — this is the latent risk the 10-K does not surface.

rfm_tuples.R: No one of the Company's customers accounted for 10% or more of the consolidated net sales during the years ended December 31, 2023, 2022 and 2021. (10-K Note Concentration of Credit Risk)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify the negative concentration claim through self-text scan and prior-year filings. Mode B: derive whether segment- or product-level concentration exists (e.g., a few hospital systems dominating CSS revenue, or private-label TT customers concentrated in one or two channel partners) that the consolidated 10% threshold masks.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Concentration of Credit Risk note + Item 1 (private-label TT business description) + edgar_fts mirror
rfm_tuples.M_value: Negative claim is consistently stated across years. 10-K Item 1 acknowledges 'private-label sales of a broad set of our regenerative and wound care technologies' in TT, and the Boston recall risk factor notes 'we are unable to predict the effect that the Boston recall will have on our relationships for such private label products,' implying private-label customers are economically material to TT but not to consolidated 10%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: a binary consolidated >10% test is non-informative when the at-risk segment is ~33% of revenue and the at-risk sub-business (private label) is a slice of that. The 10-K does not quantify private-label exposure or top-distributor exposure within TT; investors cannot triangulate the recall's customer-attrition surface from the disclosure.

rfm_tuples.R: Pembroke Pines Firefighters & Police Officers Pension Fund v. Integra LifeSciences Holdings Corporation, No. 23-cv-20321 (D.N.J.)... The Company believes that it has strong defenses to the allegations in the Pembroke Litigation, and intends to defend the matter vigorously. (Q1 2024 10-Q Note on Contingencies)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm the securities class action exists and verify whether management quantified a loss accrual or characterized loss as reasonably possible. Mode B: derive whether the period covered (March 11, 2019 to May 22, 2023) implicates the same disclosure controls and forecasting assumptions that produced the H2 2024 commercialization claim in the 10-K.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2024 10-Q Contingencies note + 10-K legal proceedings disclosure + edgar_fts mirror (Pembroke Pines + Integra returned 4 IART filings disclosing the action)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Class action filed against Company and certain current and former executive officers, alleging Section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5 violations based on 'materially false and misleading statements and omissions relating to certain quality systems issues identified by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration at the Company's Boston, Massachusetts manufacturing facility, the Company's efforts to remediate those issues, and the Company's forecasts for certain products in its Tissue Technologies segment.' No loss accrual disclosed; no range of reasonably possible loss disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the cleanest forensic finding in the file. A pension fund has explicitly alleged that prior management forecasts about Boston remediation and TT product expectations were materially misleading — and within the same period the Company has now walked back its own H2 2024 commercialization timeline (C1). The lawsuit's thesis and the realized claim-evolution evidence are pointing the same direction. Management's qualitative 'strong defenses, defend vigorously' boilerplate without an accrual range is the standard pre-trial posture, but it does not address the substantive forensic concern.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify the quantitative inputs. Mode B: derive sensitivity — at a 15% discount rate (Q1 2024), 2% terminal growth, and revenue dependent on Boston resumption, what does a one-year resumption delay (the actual Q1 2024 reality) do to headroom?

A 15% discount rate is high relative to the Company's actual cost of capital, which inflates apparent rigor but also makes the model very sensitive to revenue timing. This is the most leveraged accounting estimate on the balance sheet and the one PwC flagged as a CAM.

supplemental_signals.fda_timeline: 2019 Warning Letter (TEI/Boston); 2021 Form 483; March 2023 Form 483; May 2023 voluntary global recall of Boston-manufactured products (PriMatrix, SurgiMend, Revize, TissueMend) distributed March 2018 to May 2023; July 17 2023 Warning Letter to TEI; manufacturing resumed Q4 2023; CereLink 510(k) clearance Feb 4 2024 (separate matter); commercial distribution of Boston products NOT resumed at 3/31/2024 and management removed 2024 from the resumption window in the Q1 2024 10-Q

summary: Severity profile (P/M/S/R/U) = 2 / 5 / 2 / 0 / 1. Top findings: (1) C1/C2 — the 10-K's H2 2024 Boston commercialization target was explicitly walked back to 'not in 2024' in the very next 10-Q, with a concurrent $7.1M intangible impairment and a quantitative goodwill test on the $388.5M TT reporting unit (20% headroom). (2) C7 — Pembroke Pines securities class action alleges the same forecasting / quality-system disclosures that the Q1 2024 walkback now substantively concedes were too optimistic. (3) C3/C9 — Senior Credit Facility maximum leverage was relaxed to 4.50x through Q4 2024 specifically to absorb the recall + the $275M debt-funded Acclarent close (4/1/2024), with a step-down to 4.25x starting Q1 2025 against a revenue base that has lost Boston for the entirety of 2024. The audit posture is clean (PwC since 1989, ICFR effective, no going-concern language) and the company is not lying in the obvious smallcap-distress sense, but the framework is doing real Mode B work: management's near-term timeline for the most economically important remediation broke between Feb 28 and May 6, 2024, and the asset base (TT goodwill) and capital plan (Acclarent + ASRs) are calibrated to a recovery the Company has just begun to disown. Verdict: SHORT-tier — not a fraud, but a forensic underdelivery profile that has not been priced into the 10-K's own forward statements as of the cutoff.
